newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED SQUAD PENPIX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED SQUAD PENPIX.

text.p: Pen pictures of the Manchester United players likely to comprise the squad for Saturday's English premier league match against Liverpool at Anfield:

Peter Schmeichel. Goalkeeper. Aged 33. Despite occasional histrionics, Schmeichel is arguably the world's best goalkeeper. Giant and imposing, yet with quick reactions. A back injury could keep him out of the match.

Raimond van der Gouw. Goalkeeper. 34. Reserve who had made just three appearances for United since his arrival from Vitesse Arnhem when he was called up to replace the injured Schmeichel just before the European Cup semifinal against Borussia Dortmund. Was criticised in the English media for failing to prevent Dortmund's winner.

Denis Irwin. Right-back. 31. Reliable, consistent Republic of Ireland full-back who has played more than 300 games since joining United from Oldham in June 1990. Currently troubled by a groin injury but should be fit to play on Saturday.

Gary Pallister. Central defender. 31. A series of injuries has blighted his playing appearances this season but he now appears to be back to his best. Commanding in the air and the pivot of the United defence.

Ronnie Johnsen. Defender. 27. Norwegian who has adapted well to English soccer since joining from Turkish League club Besiktas at the start of the season. Has yet to score in the league for United but a threat at attacking set-pieces.
Gary Neville, Defender. 22. Made his England debut aged 20 in June 1995. Philip Neville's brother and an automatic first choice in the starting line-up. Fast, level-headed, intelligent defender.
Philip Neville, Defender. 20. Has recovered from the injuries which have restricted his appearances this season. Like his brother Gary an outstanding defender and an England international.

David May. Defender. 26. Central defender who seemed to have finally secured a place in the starting line-up when he injured himself recently. Scored the opening goal when United beat Porto 4-0 in the European Cup quarter-final last month but doubtful for Saturday's match.

David Beckham. Midfielder. 21. Scored the goal which gave United a 1-0 win over Liverpool when the sides met at Old Trafford in October. Has had an outstanding season and was voted Young Player of the Year and runner-up in the Player of the Year poll by his fellow professionals on Sunday.

Karel Poborsky. Midfielder. 23. Best known for his superb goal for the Czech Republic against Portugal during Euro 96. Has failed to gain a regular place in United's starting line-up and is often on the bench.

Roy Keane. Midfielder. 25. A booking in Dortmund has ruled him out of the second leg of the European Cup semifinal so he will probably be even more fired up than usual to do well against Liverpool on Saturday.
Nicky Butt. Midfielder. 22. Capped for the first time against Mexico last month, a product of United's youth system who has really matured this season.

Andy Cole. Striker. 25. Finally things are going Cole's way after two difficult years at Old Trafford. Has scored five times in his last seven starts and is playing with more confidence than at any time since his arrival from Newcastle in January 1995.

Ryan Giggs. Forward. 23. Earlier this season there were doubts that he would ever fulfil his potential. But has been on top form this season, with his devastating ball control and speed causing opponents continual problems. The most naturally-gifted player in Britain.

Eric Cantona. Forward. 30. Scored the winning goal against Liverpool in last season's F.A. Cup Final which secured United's double. This season he has not matched the heights he reached last year when he was voted England's Footballer of the Year.
Paul Scholes. Striker. 21. Highly-promising talented goalscorer who has to be content with a place in the squad rather than a guarantee of a place in the team.
Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Striker. 24. The discovery of the season. Joined United in the summer as a long-term investment from Norwegian side Molde but has made a huge impact, scoring 14 goals.
Jordi Cruyff. Forward. 23. Son of Johan who moved to United from Barcelona after Euro 96. Has had a frustrating season, making only three appearances in the last four months.

Brian McClair. Forward. 33. Has been at United for 10 seasons and celebrated that with a testimonial match against his old club Celtic at Old Trafford on Tuesday. Widely respected for his graft and effective linkplay, even at 33 is a valued member of Alex Ferguson's squad.
